policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere וְקָדְשֵׁי is a construct plural (C/Ncmpc) with no suffix, which makes the following בֵּית יְהוָה its nomen rectum: "and the holy things of the house of Jehovah." Ketiv וקדשו is singular with a 3ms suffix (C/Ncmsc/Sp3ms), "and his holy things," leaving בֵּית יְהוָה free to complete the verb. The ASV takes the second path on both counts: it reads "he brought into the house of Jehovah ... and the things that himself had dedicated," attaching the house to וַיָּבֵא and supplying a reflexive possessor the qere has no morpheme for. The suffix is visible in the English, so the ketiv is selected.

Qere הַמֶּלֶךְ carries the article (Td/Ncmsa), ketiv מלך does not (Ncmsa); same lemma (4428) and same word in the construct chain בֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ, "the treasures of the king's house." English marks the possessor of a construct chain with "the" whether or not the Hebrew is formally definite, and no ASV note is mapped to the word, so the wording cannot separate the readings. Underdetermined; the base qere stands.
